content: 1. Avoid or Use Alternate Drug: The pretomanid regimen is associated with hepatotoxicity. Patients should avoid alcohol and other hepatotoxic agents, including herbal supplements and drugs, except for bedaquiline and linezolid. 2. Serious Interaction Use Alternate Drug: Both primaquine and erythromycin lactobionate increase the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. 3. Serious Interaction Use Alternate Drug: Primidone decreases the level or effect of erythromycin lactobionate by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Additionally, primidone increases the elimination of erythromycin lactobionate, leading to reduced drug levels. This interaction is considered minor but should still be monitored. 4. Contraindicated: Erythromycin lactobionate and procainamide both increase the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of significant cardiac effects. 5. Serious Interaction Use Alternate Drug: Prochlorperazine and erythromycin lactobionate both increase the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. 6. Serious Interaction Use Alternate Drug: Promazine and erythromycin lactobionate both increase the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. 7. Serious Interaction Use Alternate Drug: Promethazine and erythromycin lactobionate both increase the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. 8. Monitor Closely: Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of propafenone by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 9. Serious Interaction Use Alternate Drug: Erythromycin lactobionate increases the effects of protamine by decreasing its metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. 10. Serious Interaction Use Alternate Drug: Protriptyline and erythromycin lactobionate both increase the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. 11. Monitor Closely: Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the level or effect of pyridoxine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 12. Monitor Closely: Erythromycin lactobionate increases the toxicity of quetiapine by prolonging the QTc interval. Co-administration with drugs that prolong the QT interval or in patients with risk factors for QT prolongation should be avoided. If co-administration is necessary, close monitoring with ECG is recommended. 13. Contraindicated: Quinidine and erythromycin lactobionate both increase the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of significant cardiac effects. 14. Serious Interaction Use Alternate Drug: Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of quinidine by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. 15. Monitor Closely: Erythromycin lactobionate and quinine both increase the QTc interval. Erythromycin lactobionate also increases the level or effect of quinine by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 16. Serious Interaction Use Alternate Drug: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases the levels of erythromycin lactobionate by decreasing its metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 17. Monitor Closely: Erythromycin lactobionate and quizartinib both increase the effects of each other by prolonging the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely, including frequent ECG monitoring. 18. Minor Interaction: Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of rabeprazole by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 19. Monitor Closely: Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of ramelteon by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 20. Monitor Closely: Erythromycin lactobionate and ranolazine both increase the QTc interval. Erythromycin lactobionate also increases the level or effect of ranolazine by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. 21. Serious Interaction Use Alternate Drug: Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of repaglinide by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. 22. Serious Interaction Use Alternate Drug: Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of repotrectinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. 23. Serious Interaction Use Alternate Drug: Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of resmetirom by other mechanisms (refer to comments). Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. Resmetirom, an OATP1B1/3 substrate, should not be co-administered with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors.
